items.title: THE 10 BEST CODING IDES IN THE AGE OF CODEX AND CLAUDE CODE
items.summary:
THE 10 BEST CODING IDES IN THE AGE OF CODEX AND CLAUDE CODE

A coding IDE  is no longer only a place you type. OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code run as terminal agents that read a repo, edit files, run tests and open pull requests. The editor's job is to host those agents, show diffs you can trust, and keep debugging and review close to the code.

This list ranks ten editors for that job. Official prices and docs were checked on November 11, 2026. Adoption figures are from the Stack Overflow 2026 Developer Survey, published October 6, with 30,903 valid responses. On the IDE question (n = 13,193), Visual Studio Code was used regularly by 70.9% of respondents. On the coding-agent question (n = 12,255), 65.5% had used Claude Code in the past year and 58.7% had used GitHub Copilot, ahead of OpenAI Codex at 29.5% and Cursor at 25.5%. Multiple answers were allowed, so these shares are reach, not exclusive market share, and the sample is self-selected. Of respondents who use coding assistants or agents, 73% use them daily.

Codex is included in ChatGPT plans. Free and Go ($8 a month) have limited access. Plus at $20 a month is the practical starting point for the CLI, the IDE extension, the desktop app and Codex on the web. Pro starts at $100 a month, and you can also pay per token with an API key. Current models include the GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 families (Sol, Terra, Luna and Astra), plus earlier GPT-5.6 variants.

Claude Code is included with Claude Pro at $20 a month, or $17 a month if you pay $200 a year up front, and with Max at $100 and Ultra at $200. It is not on the Free plan. Pro includes Opus, Sonnet and Haiku. Fable is billed with usage credits on Pro, and is included up to half the weekly limit on Max and Ultra. Claude Code 2.1.321, shipped November 9, made Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) the default Fable model, with a 1M-token context. Official integrations exist for VS Code and its forks, and for JetBrains IDEs. Everywhere else, run claude in the terminal.

The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) lets an editor host Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode and similar harnesses in a panel. Zed and JetBrains Air are the clearest ACP hosts.

📊 Comparison at a glance

Prices are US-dollar list prices, before tax, as of November 11, 2026. "Paid from" is the cheapest individual plan usable for daily agent work, not the free tier.

| Rank | Editor | Paid from | Codex | Claude Code | SO IDE use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Cursor | $30 Premium (third-party models) | Official extension | Official extension | 14.9% |
| 2 | VS Code + Copilot | $10 Copilot Pro | Official extension | Official extension | 70.9% |
| 3 | JetBrains IDEs + AI | $10 AI Pro, plus IDE license | Air / AI Chat | Official plugin + CLI | IntelliJ 24.3% |
| 4 | Zed | $0 with your own agents, or $10 Pro | ACP registry | ACP registry | 11.4% |
| 5 | Google Antigravity | $0, or Google AI Pro | Not a first-party host | Not a first-party host | 0.4% |
| 6 | Devin Desktop | $20 Pro | Official extension + ACP | Official extension + ACP | Windsurf 3.2% |
| 7 | Kiro | $20 Pro | Models + terminal CLI | Official extension | 2.8% |
| 8 | Neovim | $0, plus your agent plan | Terminal, community plugins | Terminal, community plugins | 14.7% |
| 9 | Xcode | $0 on macOS | Built-in agent (26.3) | Built-in Claude Agent (26.3) | 10.0% |
| 10 | Warp | $20 Build ($18 billed yearly) | First-class CLI host | First-class CLI host | 5.2% as an agent |

Antigravity's 0.4% IDE figure and 16.0% agent figure come from different survey questions. Windsurf was renamed Devin Desktop on June 2, 2026, during the survey window of June 23 to August 5.

1. Cursor

Cursor is a Visual Studio Code fork with its own agent, Tab completion, cloud agents, automations and a code-review bot (Bugbot). In the survey it was the sixth most used editor at 14.9%, and 25.5% of agent-question respondents had used it as a coding assistant. It is number one because it is still the most complete AI editor if you want agents, inline edits and a VS Code-shaped workspace in one app, and you can install the official Codex and Claude Code extensions beside Cursor's own agent.

Price: Free has limited agent and chat use. Plus is $8 a month ($80 a year) and includes only Cursor's own models: Grok 4.7, Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5 and Composer 2.5. Premium is $30 a month ($300 a year) and is the first plan that unlocks Claude, GPT and Gemini, billed at API list price from prepaid credit. Super is $100 a month, Ultra is $200, and Teams seats start at $30.

AI features: a multi-file agent, Tab and inline edits, codebase chat, cloud agents, automations and Bugbot on Premium and above. Third-party models on Premium and above include Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable, GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna, and Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon (Carbon has introductory API pricing in Cursor's docs through November 30).

Codex and Claude Code: Anthropic documents a direct Cursor install of the same Claude Code extension used in VS Code. OpenAI documents the Codex IDE extension for Cursor, signed in with ChatGPT or an API key.

Best for: VS Code users who want the deepest built-in agent editor and will pay Premium if they want Claude or GPT inside Cursor's own UI.

Weakness: Plus is Grok-only, and third-party models are metered from the first request. OpenAI's help center says it plans to wind down the contract that supplies OpenAI models to Cursor, and has proposed a transition period of November 12, 2026. The official end date is not yet confirmed. Documented workarounds are a bring-your-own OpenAI API key for local Chat and Agent, the Codex IDE extension, or a compatible gateway. Bring-your-own-key does not cover Cursor Tab, Auto, Cloud Agents, automations or the Cursor CLI.

2. Visual Studio Code, with Copilot and the official agent extensions

VS Code is still the default editor. It is free, including for commercial use, and 70.9% of survey respondents used it regularly. GitHub Copilot is an extension, not a fork, and was used by 58.7% of agent-question respondents, second only to Claude Code. Both labs ship official integrations here first, so VS Code is the reference host, and Copilot is the lowest-cost full assistant that stays in the editor you already have.

Price: the editor is $0. Copilot Free has limited chat and agent use, with auto model selection only. Copilot Pro is $10 a month and includes $15 of GitHub AI Credits (1,000 base credits plus a $5 flex allotment that GitHub may change). Completions are unmetered on paid plans. Pro+ is $39 a month ($70 of credits). Max is $100 ($200 of credits). Business is $19 per granted seat per month (1,900 credits per user). Enterprise is $39 (3,900 credits). One GitHub AI Credit equals $0.01, which is not the same unit as a JetBrains AI Credit.

AI features: inline completions, agent mode, Copilot CLI, pull-request review, and Copilot in the cloud. Pro+ and Max can delegate cloud work to third-party agents, including Claude and OpenAI Codex, marked as Preview. The model list includes Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus and Sonnet 5.5; availability varies by plan. Paid individual plans have a 30% Copilot Fusion model-cost discount through November 30, 2026, per GitHub's billing docs.

Codex and Claude Code: install the official Codex extension and the official Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code) and sign in with your ChatGPT or Claude plan. You can run all three in the same window. Running claude in the integrated terminal still needs the standalone CLI.

Best for: teams on GitHub, and anyone who wants official Codex and Claude Code support without switching forks.

Weakness: the deepest Claude or GPT harness is still the lab's extension or CLI, so you may run two or three panels. Credit math is easy to misread because base and flex allotments are listed separately.

3. JetBrains IDEs, with AI Assistant, Junie and Air

IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider and Android Studio remain the standard for language-aware refactoring and debugging. IntelliJ IDEA alone was used by 24.3% of survey respondents; other JetBrains IDEs appear throughout the top 20, and those shares cannot be added together. JetBrains AI was used by 12.8% of agent-question respondents. If your team lives in IntelliJ or PyCharm, a VS Code fork is a step down in refactoring quality, and JetBrains now hosts the same agents inside that tooling.

Price: the IDE is a paid subscription (student, startup and nonprofit discounts apply). AI is a separate add-on. Official docs list individual AI Pro at $10 a month with 10 AI credits per 30 days, and AI Ultimate at $30 with 35 credits. Each JetBrains AI Credit equals $1 of model usage, 100 times a GitHub AI Credit. The same help page also lists $20 / 20 credits and $60 / 70 credits in a second table for organization migrations, so confirm the org price on the JetBrains store. Air Business is $20 per AI seat per month on top of a free Basic plan.

AI features: AI Assistant for chat and completion, Junie as JetBrains' own coding agent (it uses the IDE's inspections, refactorings and test runner), and Air as the environment that can run agents in the working tree, a Git worktree or a Docker container. Air bundles Junie, Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi and GitHub Copilot.

Codex and Claude Code: Anthropic's official "Claude Code [Beta]" plugin runs the claude CLI in the IDE terminal and connects diffs and selections. OpenAI documents JetBrains support by opening AI Chat and selecting Codex. Air can also attach both over ACP, but a Claude subscription does not authorize Claude Agent in that chat surface; for subscription billing, run Claude Code in the terminal tab. ACP agents do not need a JetBrains AI subscription if you bring your own login or key.

Best for: JVM, Python, web and .NET teams that will not leave IntelliJ, PyCharm, Rider or Android Studio.

Weakness: two bills (IDE plus AI), a credit system that is easy to confuse with GitHub's, and a split between Anthropic's plugin, JetBrains' Claude Agent and the terminal CLI.

4. Zed

Zed is a GPU-accelerated, open-source editor written in Rust (GPL-3.0) for macOS, Windows and Linux. It was used regularly by 11.4% of survey respondents, and 57.3% of people who had used it wanted to keep using it. It belongs here if you already pay for Claude Code or Codex and want a fast native shell around them, without a second AI-editor subscription.

Price: Personal is $0 forever and includes the full editor plus unlimited use of your own API keys or external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex. Hosted edit predictions on the free plan are capped; confirm the live FAQ for the monthly limit. Pro is $10 a month, with unlimited edit predictions and $5 of hosted tokens, then overage at API list price plus 10%. Business is $30 per seat per month for org policies.

AI features: the Agent Panel runs Zed's own agent on hosted models, your keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter and others) or local models. The ACP registry lists Claude Agent, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Pi, each billed by its own vendor.

Codex and Claude Code: install Claude Agent or Codex from the ACP registry and start a thread in the Agent Panel. An Anthropic key set up for Zed's built-in agent does not pay for Claude Agent. You can also run either CLI in Zed's terminal.

Best for: people who want a fast open-source editor and the freedom to keep billing with Anthropic or OpenAI.

Weakness: the extension library is much smaller than VS Code's, and Windows support is newer than the macOS and Linux builds.

5. Google Antigravity

Antigravity is Google's agent-first platform: a desktop app, an IDE, a CLI, and official extensions for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Zed, Xcode and Eclipse. On November 10, 2026, Google rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon in the app, CLI and IDE extensions for Google AI Ultra subscribers, and previewed /swarm for multi-agent work. It is the most generous $0 way to run an agent IDE, and the native home of Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon. 16.0% of agent-question respondents had used it, though only 0.4% ticked it as a regular IDE.

Price: individuals can start at $0 with a personal Google account. The free plan includes a variety of agent models, unlimited Tab completions and Command requests, and basic weekly rate limits. Higher limits ride on a Google AI subscription. Google AI Pro is listed at $19.99 a month in the US and includes expanded Antigravity access and Gemini 4 Argon. Google AI Ultra starts at $99.99 a month in the US ($199.99 for the higher Ultra tier) and is the plan Google is using for Gemini 4 Carbon. Official docs say there is currently no bring-your-own-key option.

AI features: agents work across the editor, the terminal and a Chrome profile, and they report back with artifacts such as plans, walkthroughs, screenshots and browser recordings.

Codex and Claude Code: Antigravity is not an official host for those two CLIs. Ultra plans get third-party models inside Antigravity's own picker, which is not the same as running the Codex or Claude Code harness. You can still run either CLI in the terminal.

Best for: people who want a capable free agent IDE, or who already pay for Google AI Pro or Ultra.

Weakness: no BYOK, the newest Gemini models are gated to paid Google AI plans, and account and country limits apply.

6. Devin Desktop, formerly Windsurf

Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop on June 2, 2026. The editor is still a VS Code-class fork and now opens on an Agent Command Center, a board of local and cloud agent sessions. A September 8 changelog entry said Cascade was removed and Devin Local is now the built-in agent. It belongs here as the Windsurf successor, built around running several local and cloud agents, including third-party ACP agents, under one account.

Price: Free includes a light agent quota, limited models, and unlimited Tab completions and inline edits. Pro is $20 a month and adds higher quotas, frontier models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and SpaceXAI, plus open-source models, free use of SWE-2, Devin Cloud, and extra usage at API pricing. Max is $200 a month. Teams is $80 a month plus $40 per full dev seat, for up to 100 users. Pro, Max and Teams can use your ChatGPT plan.

AI features: Devin Local, Devin Cloud, the Command Center, and ACP for third-party agents.

Codex and Claude Code: OpenAI still lists Windsurf alongside VS Code and Cursor as an official Codex extension target. Anthropic says the Claude Code extension installs in Devin Desktop from Open VSX. ACP is the other path for Codex, Claude Agent and OpenCode.

Best for: teams that want Devin's cloud agent and a local editor on one bill, and people who manage many agent sessions at once.

Weakness: the rename still splits docs and forum answers between Windsurf and Devin Desktop. The free agent quota is light, so daily agent work means Pro. Survey usage was modest: Windsurf 3.2% as an IDE, 6.5% as an agent, and Devin 2.9% as an agent.

7. Kiro

Kiro is Amazon Web Services' agentic IDE, also available as a CLI, on the web and on iOS. It is built around spec-driven development: a prompt becomes requirements, a design and a task list, and the agent works through the tasks after you approve them. It supports Open VSX extensions and can import VS Code settings. 2.8% of survey respondents used it regularly as an IDE, and it is the only widely shipped editor that makes a written spec the default path.

Price: Free is perpetual and includes 50 credits a month, with open-weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5, subject to rate limits. Pro is $20 a month; official proration examples work out to 1,000 included credits. Pro+ is $40, Pro Max is $100 and Power is $200, with Power officially listed at 10,000 credits. Independent trackers also list 2,000 credits on Pro+ and 5,000 on Pro Max; confirm those figures on https://t.co/xzAe1BA4zH before you budget. Add-on credits are $0.04 each. Team credit-pool seats are $20 a month and add 500 shared credits per seat.

AI features: spec mode, hooks, and a CLI and web/iOS surface that share the same harness. Default routing is Auto. Paid plans include GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. There is no bring-your-own-key path on the public pricing page.

Codex and Claude Code: the official Claude Code extension can be installed from Open VSX. Codex is available as a model family inside Kiro, which is not the same as the Codex CLI harness. You can run either CLI in the terminal.

Best for: AWS-centric teams, and anyone who wants a design approved before the agent writes code.

Weakness: the free credit grant is small, and premium models burn credits faster. Content from free and individual users may be used to improve the service unless you opt out, a weaker default than Cursor with Privacy Mode on.

8. Neovim

Neovim is a free, open-source, modal editor (Apache 2.0) with built-in LSP support. 14.7% of survey respondents used it regularly, almost identical to Cursor's 14.9%. Among people who had already used it, 69.9% wanted to keep using it, one of the highest admiration scores in the IDE table. You run claude or codex in a split and stay on SSH, tmux and servers where a GUI fork will not go.

Price: $0 for the editor. You pay only for Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or API usage. Copilot has an official Neovim integration.

AI features: there is no first-party Neovim agent from Anthropic or OpenAI. Community plugins such as coder/claudecode.nvim and Avante.nvim fill the gap. Copilot provides official completions and chat. Review community plugins before you install them; none is an official Anthropic or OpenAI product.

Codex and Claude Code: the supported official path is the CLI in :terminal. Claude Code has a vim mode under /config.

Best for: terminal-first developers, remote servers, and people who already have a Neovim config they will not abandon.

Weakness: no official Claude Code or Codex GUI plugin. You assemble the experience yourself, and you own the breakage when APIs change.

9. Xcode

Xcode is Apple's IDE for macOS, iOS, iPadOS, watchOS and visionOS, and it is free on a Mac. 10.0% of survey respondents used it regularly. Since Xcode 26.3 (macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later), Apple has shipped built-in coding agents. For Apple-platform work, Interface Builder, SwiftUI previews, simulators and signing are still unique, and that stack now hosts Claude Agent and Codex inside the IDE.

Price: the IDE is free. Agent usage bills through the account you attach in Settings > Intelligence > Agents.

AI features: Apple's Intelligence panel can install Claude Agent, built on the Claude Agent SDK, and Codex as a built-in agent. Agents can edit project files, change settings, build, and check work in Previews.

Codex and Claude Code: OpenAI's Codex IDE docs say to open the coding assistant, start a chat and choose Codex. Apple also exposes Xcode over MCP, so the Claude Code CLI can attach with a documented xcrun mcpbridge setup and keep the full CLI feature set. If you need skills, hooks and /rewind exactly as in the CLI, use the CLI plus MCP.

Best for: iOS and Mac developers who want agents inside the official Apple toolchain.

Weakness: it is Mac-only, and the wrong default for backend or web work.

10. Warp

Warp is a GPU-accelerated terminal that has grown into an agent workspace, with a modern input editor, inline code review, Warp Agent, cloud agents, and first-class hosting of other CLIs. It was used by 5.2% of agent-question respondents. If your daily loop is already Codex or Claude Code in a terminal, Warp adds review, notifications and remote control without forcing a VS Code fork.

Price: Free includes the terminal, Warp Agent CLI access, bring-your-own inference, and limited cloud-agent use, with extra usage at pay-as-you-go rates. Build is $20 a month, or $18 a month billed annually, and includes $20 of agent usage at API rates plus full Warp Agent access. Max includes $200 of agent usage a month. Business is $45 per user per month ($20 of usage per seat) with SSO, for up to 25 seats.

AI features: Warp Agent, mixed-model routing, and a published model set that includes Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3.

Codex and Claude Code: Warp auto-detects both CLIs in a pane and adds a rich input editor, code-review comments, attach-as-context, vertical-tab status and Remote Control. Third-party CLIs stay in their terminal tab rather than Warp's conversation panel.

Best for: developers who live in the terminal and want Claude Code or Codex with better review and multi-pane control.

Weakness: it is not a full language IDE. You will still want a language IDE for deep debugging and large refactorings.

🧭 Which one to pick

Cursor Premium at $30 if you want Claude or GPT in Cursor's own agent; Plus at $8 if Grok and Composer are enough. Install the Claude Code and Codex extensions anyway, especially while OpenAI's Cursor-supply contract is in flux.

VS Code with Copilot Pro at $10, plus the two official extensions, is the official host and the lowest serious paid assistant. Copilot Business is $19 a seat for GitHub-centered teams.

If you will not leave IntelliJ, PyCharm, Rider or Android Studio, add Anthropic's Claude Code plugin and, if you want a JetBrains-native agent, AI Ultimate at $30, or run Junie, Claude Agent and Codex through Air with your existing lab logins.

If you already pay for Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus and want a fast open-source editor with no second AI bill, use Zed's free Personal plan and attach both agents over ACP.

If your budget is $0, start with Google Antigravity's individual plan or Copilot Free inside VS Code. Antigravity is the more generous free agent IDE. Zed's editor is free, but its hosted AI is not.

Devin Desktop Pro at $20 if you want many agents on one board, including a cloud agent. Kiro Pro at $20 if you want a written spec before code. Neovim plus the CLIs if you work on a server or in a modal config. Xcode 26.3 if you build for Apple platforms. Warp Build at $20, or Warp Free with the CLIs and your own keys, if your home is the terminal.

Pick the editor whose diffs, debugger and extensions you already trust. The agent can be swapped later more easily than that review surface.

Also worth knowing, but not in the ten: Trae, ByteDance's VS Code fork, is shipping (Free, a region-limited Lite plan at $8, then Pro $20, Pro+ $60, Ultra $200) but had only 0.7% regular IDE use. Cline and OpenCode are open-source harnesses you can drop into VS Code, JetBrains or Zed. Visual Studio remains widely used (27.6%) and has Copilot, but no official Claude Code extension; use the CLI in its terminal. Void, an open-source VS Code fork, was archived on June 2, 2026, and is no longer maintained.

Prices and model catalogs change quickly. Recheck the vendor pages below before you switch a team.

Nov 10 (Reuters) - Anthropic's blockbuster IPO will value the Claude chatbot creator ​at up to $1.4 trillion, slightly short of some investors' expectations, setting up a key test of Wall Street's faith in the AI boom it helped ignite.

The company ‌is kicking off the roadshow for a share sale expected to set a benchmark for the sector, following years of hype that fueled a massive influx of capital into AI companies and sent the US stock market to all-time highs. results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python đơn giản tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy. Hàm sẽ trả về giá trị Fibonacci cho chỉ số `n` (với `F(0) = 0` và `F(1) = 1`).  

```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.

    Tham số:
        n (int): Chỉ số của dãy Fibonacci (n >= 0).

    Trả về:
        int: Giá trị Fibonacci tại vị trí n.

    Lưu ý:
        - Đệ quy thuần sẽ có độ phức tạp O(2^n), nên chỉ thích hợp cho n
          nhỏ (thường < 30). Đối với n lớn hơn, nên dùng memoization
          hoặc phương pháp lặp để tránh tính lại các giá trị.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    # Đệ quy: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng
if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Giải thích nhanh**  
- Các trường hợp cơ sở (`n == 0` và `n == 1`) trả về giá trị đã biết.  
- Với các giá trị lớn hơn, hàm gọi lại chính nó để tính `F(n‑1)` và `F(n‑2)`, sau đó cộng lại.  

Nếu bạn cần tính các giá trị lớn hơn một cách hiệu quả hơn, có thể bổ sung **memoization** (lưu trữ các kết quả đã tính) hoặc chuyển sang thuật toán lặp. Nếu muốn mình viết phiên bản có memoization, cứ cho mình biết nhé!
